question: what is the melting point of the tungsten filament used in bulbs?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3422ºC**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The melting point of tungsten is **3422ºC**, making it one of the highest melting points of all metals.
 
• This property allows tungsten filaments to operate at high temperatures without melting, which is crucial for their use in incandescent light bulbs.
 
• Tungsten's high melting point contributes to its ability to emit bright light when heated.
 
• In addition to light bulbs, tungsten is also used in various high-temperature applications such as rocket engine nozzles, heating elements, and welding electrodes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Incandescent Light Bulbs**

 
 
• These bulbs produce light by heating a tungsten filament until it glows.
 
• The filament is enclosed in a glass bulb filled with an inert gas like argon to prevent the tungsten from oxidizing and burning out quickly.
 
• Despite their inefficiency compared to modern lighting technologies, incandescent bulbs are still used in some applications due to their warm light quality.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Tungsten**
 
 
• Tungsten is a chemical element with the symbol W and atomic number 74.
 
• It is known for its remarkable physical properties, including its high density (19.25 g/cm³) and high tensile strength.
 
• These properties make it suitable for applications involving extreme conditions, such as in military projectiles and high-speed cutting tools.
 
 
 
• **Other High-Melting-Point Materials**
 
 
• Materials like Tantalum (melting point: 3017ºC) and Molybdenum (melting point: 2623ºC) also have high melting points, making them useful in various high-temperature applications.
 
• These materials are often used in electronics, aerospace, and industrial processes where high thermal resistance is required.
